children: Palm oil falls in early Asian trading. Production is expected to remain strong over the next three months as the market has entered its peak-crop period, AmInvestment Bank says in a note. Meanwhile, technical analysis suggests that an uptrend in crude palm oil futures may remain intact, with any short-term pullback likely to attract buying interest, it adds. AmInvestment Bank expects palm oil prices to face resistance at 4,996 ringgit a ton. The Bursa Malaysia Derivatives contract for November delivery is down 43 ringgit at 4,933 ringgit a ton. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)
